purpose: Measure whether the trained graft contributes to held-out clean-language prediction in the exact clean checkpoints used by S1.

evaluation.pairing: The intact and bypassed evaluations use the same checkpoint, blocks, batch size, and floating-point recipe.
evaluation.intact: Normal deterministic address preparation and graft residual injection.
evaluation.bypassed: Replace the grafted decoder-layer wrapper by its stored original layer for inference; every learned backbone parameter remains unchanged.
evaluation.primary_difference: bypassed_clean_nll - intact_clean_nll; positive values mean the trained graft improves clean NLL in that checkpoint

statistics.report: all paired values, mean, median, sign count, and fixed 10000-resample paired bootstrap interval for the mean
statistics.decision: descriptive post-hoc audit; no pass/fail gate

interpretation_boundary: A positive paired difference shows that the graft is functionally used for held-out clean prediction after joint clean adaptation. It does not estimate the training-time quality advantage over a separately adapted ungrafted model and does not resolve jointly pretrained Engram behavior.
verification: validate the sealed S1 manifest and every selected clean checkpoint digest; retain per-seed values and exact code/config hashes
